boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Amelia Springs record (April 5, 1865) in the Appomattox Campaign [March-April 1865]. Davies's destruction of the wagon train at Paineville the same day is the occasion of the action. Army-wide returns, campaign-wide loss and prisoner totals, the April 9 paroles and the retreat as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen result reads 'Inconclusive' and the live 'Indecisive'. Fitzhugh Lee says the enemy were driven to within a mile of Jetersville, where the pursuit stopped; Humphreys places the attack at Amelia Springs about sunset as Davies was about to recross Flat Creek; NPS says the running fight began north of Amelia Springs and went beyond Jetersville.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The accounts place the fight differently and are not reconciled.

open_questions: Crook's, Davies's, Gregg's and Smith's reports (Nos. 208-212), Sheridan's account of the Paineville raid (selected; cited under VA088), Rosser's and Gary's accounts and the returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the commander of the Second Corps in this campaign, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; where it narrates his own corps it is a participant's account. It relies on the reports of Sheridan, Warren, Wright, Gibbon, Ewell and Fitzhugh Lee, on Confederate testimony before the Warren Court of Inquiry and on the returns, so it is not independent of those families. Lee's, Sheridan's, Bushrod Johnson's, Miles's, Gibbon's, Ewell's and Fitzhugh Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLVI, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
